verses.text: Samuel took a flask of oil, poured it on Saul's head, kissed him, and said, “The LORD has anointed you to rule over his inheritance.

When you leave me today, you'll meet two men near Rachel's tomb at Zelzah on Benjamin's border. They'll tell you the donkeys you went looking for have been found and that your father is now worried about you and asking what he should do about his son.

Then you'll go on to the oak of Tabor, where three men going up to worship God at Bethel will meet you. One will be carrying three young goats, another three loaves of bread, and another a container of wine.
They'll greet you and offer you two loaves. Take them.

After that you'll reach the hill of God, where the Philistines have a garrison. As you enter the town, you'll meet a group of prophets coming down from the high place. They'll be prophesying, with a lute, tambourine, pipe, and harp playing ahead of them.
The LORD's Spirit will come powerfully upon you. You'll prophesy with them and become a different man.
Once these signs happen, do what the situation calls for, because God is with you.
Go down to Gilgal ahead of me. I'll come down to offer burnt offerings and peace offerings. Wait seven days until I arrive and tell you what to do.”
As Saul turned to leave Samuel, God gave him a different heart. All those signs came true that day.
When Saul and his servant reached the hill, a group of prophets met him. God's Spirit came powerfully upon him, and he prophesied among them.
When everyone who'd known Saul saw him prophesying with the prophets, they asked each other, “What's happened to Kish's son? Is Saul one of the prophets too?”
A man from there asked, “And who's their father?” That's how the saying started: “Is Saul one of the prophets too?”
When Saul finished prophesying, he went to the high place.
Saul's uncle asked him and his servant, “Where did you go?” Saul answered, “To look for the donkeys. When we couldn't find them, we went to Samuel.”
His uncle said, “Please tell me what Samuel told you.”
Saul said, “He told us straight out that the donkeys had been found.” But he said nothing about what Samuel had told him about becoming king.
Samuel called the people together before the LORD at Mizpah.
He told Israel, “The LORD, the God of Israel, says, ‘I brought Israel up out of Egypt and rescued you from the Egyptians and every kingdom that oppressed you.’
But today you've rejected your God, the one who rescues you from all your troubles and disasters. You said, ‘No! Give us a king!’ Now present yourselves before the LORD by tribe and by clan.”
Samuel brought all Israel's tribes forward, and the tribe of Benjamin was chosen.
He brought Benjamin forward clan by clan, and the clan of Matri was chosen. Then Saul son of Kish was chosen, but when they went looking for him, they couldn't find him.
They asked the LORD again, “Has the man come here yet?” The LORD answered, “He's hiding among the baggage.”
They ran and brought him out. When he stood among the people, he was a head taller than everyone else.
Samuel asked, “Do you see the man the LORD has chosen? Nobody among the people is like him.” Everyone shouted, “Long live the king!”
Samuel explained the rules of the kingdom to the people, wrote them down in a book, and placed it before the LORD. Then he sent everyone home.
Saul went home to Gibeah too, and men whose hearts God had touched went with him.
Some troublemakers said, “How could this man save us?” They looked down on him and brought him no gift. Saul kept quiet.
